## Carl Friedrich Gauss {#ss4-gauss-story .ar-lesson .ar-gauss-story}

<p class="ar-gauss-bio"><strong>1777–1855</strong> · A German mathematician whose work shaped number theory, geometry and astronomy.</p>

<p class="ar-story-label">A famous classroom story — the details are uncertain.</p>

In one popular version, young Gauss is misbehaving. To keep him busy, his teacher tells him to add all the integers from $1$ to $100$.

Almost immediately, Gauss gives his answer:

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
$$5050$$

<p class="ar-story-question">How did he do it?</p>

:::

::: notes

Allow about one minute. Present this explicitly as a popular classroom story, not a verified account of Gauss being punished. The earliest known account, published by Sartorius von Waltershausen in 1856, describes Gauss quickly summing an arithmetic series but does not specify 1 to 100 or the pairing method. Later versions add details. “Apocryphal” here means historically uncertain, not proven fictional. Give students a moment to imagine a shortcut, then continue to Example 4.1 without explaining the pairing yet.

Biography: MacTutor, University of St Andrews, https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Gauss/ . Historical discussion: Brian Hayes, “Gauss’s Day of Reckoning”, American Scientist 94 (2006), 200–205, https://eclass.uoa.gr/modules/document/file.php/MATH417/Bibliografia/HayesGaussDayofReckoning.pdf .

:::
